Raising learners in excellence and godly character
Welcome toSt James Hatcham CE School
On behalf of our pupils, staff and governors, it is my great pleasure to welcome you to St James Hatcham Church of England Nursery and Primary School.
St James Hatcham is a vibrant, ambitious and deeply caring Christian school where excellence, opportunity and belonging sit at the heart of everything we do. From our youngest children in Acorns Nursery through to Year 6, we are committed to providing an education that is excellent, exciting and full of possibility.
Our Christian vision of ‘Raising learners in excellence and godly character’, together with our values of Love, Peace, Hope and Joy, shapes a community in which children are known, valued, challenged and encouraged to flourish.
We are proud of our strong academic outcomes, rich curriculum, specialist provision, educational visits, clubs and enrichment opportunities, alongside the exceptional pastoral care that helps our children grow into confident, articulate and compassionate young people.
As Executive Headteacher, I am privileged to work alongside Ms R H Matthews, Head of School, our dedicated staff, governors, families and wider community as we build on St James Hatcham’s strong foundations and look confidently towards its future.
At St James Hatcham, we want every child to know: you belong here, your voice matters, your talents are worth discovering and your future is full of possibility.
Sophia Bryan-WhyteExecutive Headteacher

pageCache.text:
Spirituality And Collective Worship
Collective Worship
A core part of the St James Hatcham ethos and experience
At St James Hatcham, collective worship is a vital and enriching part of daily life, rooted in the Christian vision and values of the Church of England. It offers time for the whole school community to come together to reflect, celebrate, and learn about the Christian faith.
These times of worship, along with regular prayers that take place throughout the day, helps to establish our core values and spiritual growth. It allows us to explore themes that encourage the fruits of the spirit, and to reflect on how God's teachings impact us in our day-to-day lives.
Collective worship is key to nurturing the spiritual, moral, social, and cultural development of every child, helping them to grow into caring, responsible citizens.
Ms. Price leads a Monday morning assembly to encourage children to be mindful of the school’s Christian values as they head into the school week.
Our Collective worship timetable
Our 2026 SIAMS Report
Statutory Inspection of Anglican and Methodist Schools (SIAMS) Report
We are delighted to share the results of our latest SIAMS inspection, which took place in February 2026. The inspection concluded that St James Hatcham Church of England Primary School is successfully living up to its foundation as a Church school and is enabling both our pupils and adults to flourish.
Our Vision in Action
At the heart of our school is a Christian vision rooted in love, peace, hope, and joy. We strive to nurture curious minds and godly character, ensuring that every child is inspired to "shine". The inspector noted that this vision is deeply embedded in our school, shaping our culture, relationships, and every decision we make.
Key Highlights from the Report
Exceptionally Inclusive Practice: Our commitment to inclusion ensures that every child—regardless of their starting point or background—is valued and empowered to achieve their full potential.
A Nurturing Environment: Relationships across the school are highly positive. Leaders prioritize holistic wellbeing and mental health, utilizing restorative approaches to support emotional growth and resilience.
Spiritual Flourishing: Collective worship is described as a joyful, creative, and spiritually enriching time that encourages thoughtful reflection for the whole school community.
Strong Academic Status of RE: Religious Education holds a strong status at our school, effectively developing pupils’ understanding of world faiths and encouraging them to "disagree well" with clarity and respect.
As a school community, we are committed to continuous growth. We will be focusing on deepening our pupils’ understanding of the practice of justice, helping them to recognize the wider impact of their actions as they exercise their responsibilities as global citizens.
"A genuine belief that every child is created with God-given worth permeates policy and practice." — SIAMS Report, 2026.

Vision and Values
Vision and Values
Our Vision
"In love, peace, hope and joy, we nurture curious minds and godly character, inspiring every child to shine, rooted in God's grace".
Mission Statement
We are committed to creating a happy, caring and enriching learning environment, underpinned by Christian values, most notably – joy, peace, hope and love. We celebrate children’s achievement and spiritual development; encouraging acts of kindness and consideration, mutual respect and forgiveness.
Values
We have four Christian values which we strive to live out in our everyday lives: Love, Peace, Hope and Joy.
We believe that the most important thing is to show Love for one another.
Hope is working with God.
Peace is what we bring.
These values are displayed around the school and incorporated into our school assembly themes and during the school day, extending throughout our curriculum:
RE (Pupil Experience - Curriculum menu tab)
Pupil Voice
Giving our pupils platforms to develop a strong voice helps them build confidence, learn responsibility, and understand the importance of their perspectives.
St James Hatcham is a Voice 21 school with the development of oracy skills being a common, underpinning factor across our curriculum, classroom culture, extra-curriculars and day-to-day interactions.
Pupils feel confident and comfortable in voicing their opinions and challenging their learning in class discussions and through platforms such as the school council.
"School is very nice! Even though I am a Muslim, I get to learn lots of stuff!" - Fatoumata, Year 6.
"Ms McFarlane is incredibly wonderful in RE: she is a Christian and is passionate about the subject. She helps us to understand Christianity and other religions too! There are people and places that help us to reflect and grow spiritually, like the chapel." - Aiyana, Year 6
Race Equality Pledge
The Unicef Rights of a child, Article 29 states that ‘Education …must encourage the child’s respect of human rights, as well as respect for their parents, their own and other cultures …’ We believe passionately in equality and that people, no matter what their race or culture, should be respected, valued and celebrated. pageCache.pageTitle: St James Hatcham CE School - Welcome
pageCache.text:
Welcome
Welcome from the Executive Headteacher
St James Hatcham reflects a vibrant and dynamic community where every individual is celebrated, championed and empowered to succeed.
On behalf of our pupils, staff and governors, it is my great pleasure to welcome you to St James Hatcham Church of England Nursery and Primary School.
St James Hatcham is a vibrant, ambitious and deeply caring Christian school with a proud history, a strong sense of community and high aspirations for every child. It is a school with much to celebrate: excellent educational outcomes, committed staff, wonderful children and a rich range of opportunities that help our pupils to grow academically, socially, spiritually and personally.
Our ambition is simple: we want every child who joins St James Hatcham to experience an education that is excellent, exciting and full of possibility.
Excellence and opportunity
We are proud of the high standards achieved by our pupils and of our strong reputation for preparing children exceptionally well for the next stage of their education.
Academic excellence, however, is only part of the St James experience.
We believe that a great primary education should open children’s eyes to the world around them, develop their confidence and curiosity, and help them discover talents and interests that may shape their futures.
Through inspirational teaching, specialist provision, educational visits, extensive clubs and enrichment opportunities, and connections with local, national and international organisations, our children are encouraged to explore, participate, question, create and achieve.
From our youngest children in Acorns Nursery through to our Year 6 pupils preparing to move on to secondary education, we want every learner to experience a rich and ambitious curriculum that develops strong foundations while also inspiring them to think beyond what they already know.
Communication and oracy are an important part of this work. We want our children to find their voices, express their ideas confidently, listen thoughtfully to others and grow into articulate young people who understand that their contribution matters.
Raising learners in excellence and godly character
At the heart of St James Hatcham is our Christian vision: 'Raising learners in excellence and godly character.'
Our Christian values of Love, Peace, Hope and Joy shape the culture of our school and the relationships within it.
These values are not simply words displayed around our building. They influence how we treat one another, how we respond when things are difficult, how we celebrate success and how we help our children understand their responsibilities to themselves, to others and to the wider world.
Our most recent SIAMS inspection recognised the strength of our deeply embedded Christian vision, our inclusive practice and the positive relationships that enable pupils and adults to flourish.
We want every child at St James Hatcham to feel known, valued, safe and that they belong.
Strong pastoral care sits alongside high expectations. We know our children well and seek to understand their individual strengths, interests and needs. We encourage them to become confident, compassionate and resilient young people who are proud of who they are and ambitious about who they can become.
An exciting chapter for St James Hatcham
I am delighted and privileged to serve as Executive Headteacher of St James Hatcham and St Luke’s Church of England Primary School.
I come to this role with enormous respect for the history, traditions and achievements of St James Hatcham and for the generations of pupils, families, staff, governors and members of the church and wider community who have helped shape the school.
My responsibility is to build confidently upon those strong foundations while ensuring that St James continues to develop, innovate and provide the very best possible education for its children.
I work closely with Ms R H Matthews, Head of School, our leadership team and our dedicated staff. Together, we share a clear commitment to maintaining high standards, strengthening professional practice and ensuring that every decision we make is rooted in what will make the greatest difference for our children.
Our leadership of St James is characterised by high expectations, shared responsibility and a determination that the school should continue to flourish.
Acorns Nursery – growing our St James family
The development of Acorns Nursery marks an exciting new chapter in the life of St James Hatcham.
Welcoming children from the age of two allows us to begin building relationships with children and their families at the very beginning of their educational journey.
These earliest years matter enormously.
Our ambition is for Acorns to provide an exceptional early childhood experience: a place filled with warmth, purposeful play, language, exploration and joyful learning.
Children should develop secure relationships with the adults who care for them, become confident communicators, learn to explore their environment and begin developing the curiosity and independence that will support everything that follows.
Most importantly, our youngest children should know from their very first day that St James is a place where they belong.
Part of something bigger
St James Hatcham is proud to be part of the Southwark Diocesan Board of Education Multi-Academy Trust.
Being part of the Trust provides opportunities to collaborate, learn and benefit from the expertise and support of a wider family of schools, while preserving the distinctive character, heritage and close-knit community that make St James Hatcham special.
Our relationships with parents and carers are equally important.
Children thrive when families and schools work together with trust, openness and shared expectations. We therefore want parents and carers to feel welcomed into the life of the school, to know that their voices are valued and to share our ambitions for their children.
A school where children can flourish
Ultimately, the success of a school can be seen and felt in the experiences of its children.
We want St James Hatcham to be a school where children arrive each morning excited about what they might discover; where excellent teaching inspires them to think deeply; where their talents are noticed and nurtured; and where opportunities extend far beyond the classroom.
We want our pupils to leave us with strong academic foundations, excellent character and the confidence to embrace the next stage of their lives.
We want every child to know:
You are capable of achieving great things.
Your talents are worth discovering.
Your future is full of possibility.
Whether you are already part of our school family, considering St James Hatcham for your child or visiting our website to learn more about us, we hope you will discover a school that combines excellence with warmth, ambition with opportunity, and high expectations with genuine care.
On behalf of our children, staff and governors, I warmly invite you to visit St James Hatcham, meet our community and experience for yourself what makes our school so special.
There is much to be proud of at St James Hatcham. There is an exciting future ahead.
Sophia Bryan-WhyteExecutive HeadteacherSt James Hatcham CE Nursery and Primary School

Local
Goldsmiths University:
Being placed right across the road from this distinguished university creates a wonderful and wide-ranging partnership. Our teachers work closely with the Teacher Training tutors and trainee teachers are placed with us yearly to work under the direction of our most experienced teachers.
Our staff have been used as models of best practice for the Teacher Training courses. Most recently, our Year 1 class and early reading enthusiast Miss Kay demonstrated a phonics lesson during a lecture for post graduate students studying to train to teach. The teaching was described as 'inspiring' and our pupils were given a certificate to thank them for their contribution to the development of future teachers!
We have also collaborated as prestigious events such as the COP26 Climate Change Conference, where St James Hatcham partnered with the community outreach and scientists at Goldsmiths on workshops designed to highlight, teach and embed learning around climate and climate change.
CCA Gallery at Goldsmiths - school of residence:
St James Hatcham, having worked on two specialist art projects with artists supported by the CCA Gallery, have been selected to be the gallery's first school of residence. Our vision as school in residency at the gallery is to provide our children with a varied arts curriculum that enables all to encounter the abundant creative culture this world has to offer.
Children will have opportunities to study a wide range of contemporary artists from across continents and from a range of traditions. Use of the contemporary art space will provide a unique, creative experience where children, inspired by the rich tapestry of artists on exhibition, can develop their own projects by altering medium, theme, scale, techniques or composition. We endeavour to broaden our school’s creative links within our local community, ensuring that the immeasurable value of arts education is recognised by staff, children and parents alike.
Bow Arts
We are lucky to collaborate with arts and education charity Bow Arts. We collaborate on projects for individual classes and they support us in Curriculum Development - take a look at the clay and printing staff CPD we have undertaken this term.

Acorns Nursery Places Available!
Acorns Nursery Places Available!

Acorns Nursery Application form 2026
Our nursery forms an integral part of our Foundation Stage provision, giving children a wonderful head start through expert early years education and leadership. This seamless path from nursery into reception classes is proven to boost lifelong learning skills and emotional wellbeing. Children thrive in their own dedicated, well-equipped nursery room and private outdoor play area, alongside access to our exciting new forest school environment, a broad and enriching early years curriculum, and wider school play spaces.
Operating as a school-based nursery, our unified team delivers a continuous learning path and a smooth, reassuring transition across the vital early years of a child’s development from ages 2 to 7.
We offer funded places through the Free Early Education Entitlement for eligible children, as well as the Extended Funding Entitlement. To secure extended provision, families must provide St James Hatcham with their details. Please note that extended childcare requires reconfirmation with HMRC every 3 months. HMRC typically sends out reminders, but failing to reapply before the deadline and grace period expires means funding will be affected.
Families can check their eligibility online at gov.uk/apply-30-hours-free-childcare. You will need your National Insurance number or UTR (if self-employed) to complete the check.
Fees and Session Rates (Effective September 2026)
The standard hourly rate for both 2 and 3-year-olds is set at £9.02 per hour.
For children eligible for 15 funded hours who wish to attend full-time, the charge for the additional 15 hours is £135.30 per week.
For children not yet entitled to funded hours who would like to secure a 15-hour place (either morning or afternoon), the fee is £135.30 per week.
For children not eligible for funding who require a full-time place, the fee is £270 per week.
Sessions
Daily Routine & Practical Information
Lunchtime: Nursery children are asked to bring a healthy packed lunch from home. While we do not charge families separately for lunchtime supervision, please note that wraparound care and extracurricular activities are currently not offered to nursery pupils.
Uniform: Our nursery children wear a smart and comfortable uniform consisting of a white polo shirt, burgundy joggers, and black or white shoes.
Early Years Pupil Premium (EYPP)
In addition to meeting the national eligibility criteria listed below, children must attend our nursery for at least one full day to qualify for Early Years Pupil Premium funding:
Income-based Jobseeker’s Allowance
Income-related Employment and Support Allowance
Support under Part VI of the Immigration and Asylum Act 1999
The guaranteed element of Pension Credit
Child Tax Credit (provided you are not also entitled to Working Tax Credit and have an annual gross income of no more than £16,190)
Working Tax Credit run-on (paid for 4 weeks after you stop qualifying for Working Tax Credit)
Universal Credit (if you apply on or after 1 April 2018, your household income must be less than £7,400 a year after tax and not including any benefits you receive)
What EYPP Entitles Your Child To
Qualifying for the Early Years Pupil Premium (EYPP) provides additional government funding directly to St James Hatcham nursery—specifically £1.15 per hour per eligible child (up to a maximum of 570 hours per year, equating to approximately £655.50 annually for a child taking up their full 15 universal funded hours).
While this funding is paid directly to the school to support our setting, it directly benefits your child's experience by entitling them to:
Enhanced Learning & Development Support: Extra resources, specialized learning materials, and targeted educational activities tailored to help close any attainment gaps early.
Specialized Well-being Provision: Access to tailored emotional, social, or communication support tools to boost their school readiness and emotional wellbeing.
Targeted Enrichment: Enriched classroom experiences designed by our early years team to support your child's specific developmental milestones during their crucial first steps in education.
Moving Up from Nursery to Reception
Transitioning from our nursery into reception is an exciting milestone designed to be seamless, supportive, and reassuring for both children and their families. Because our nursery is an embedded part of the school's Foundation Stage, our children already share the same nurturing environment, routines, and familiar staff, helping them feel completely at home as they grow.
Throughout the summer term before starting reception, we introduce a series of carefully planned transition steps—including visits to the reception classrooms, story sessions with reception teachers, and shared playtimes—to ensure every child feels confident and ready for their next step.
Please note: Spaces for our nursery and reception progression are in exceptionally high demand, and availability is strictly limited. We strongly advise families to secure their child's place early to avoid disappointment.
For full details regarding the formal application process, key deadlines, and admission criteria, please visit our admissions page: Admissions

Governance at St James Hatcham
Governance at St James Hatcham
Strong governance is an important part of ensuring that St James Hatcham continues to provide an excellent education rooted in its Christian vision and values.
St James Hatcham Church of England Nursery and Primary School is an academy within the Southwark Diocesan Board of Education Multi-Academy Trust (SDBE MAT).
The SDBE MAT Board of Trustees is the legally accountable body for the Trust and its academies. The Trust Board delegates specified responsibilities to a Local Governing Body (LGB) at St James Hatcham through the SDBE MAT Scheme of Delegation.
The Local Governing Body is therefore part of the wider governance structure of SDBE MAT. It is not a separate legal governing body.
The role of our Local Governing Body
Our Local Governing Body provides local knowledge, strategic oversight, support, challenge and assurance.
Within the responsibilities delegated to it by the Trust, governors consider areas including:
Governors use information from leaders, school visits, performance information, pupil and staff voice and other monitoring activities to help them understand the school's strengths and areas for continued development.
the quality of education and pupils' achievement;
safeguarding and pupil welfare;
SEND and inclusion;
attendance and behaviour;
personal development;
progress against school and Trust priorities; and
Governance and school leadership
There is an important distinction between governance and the day-to-day leadership and management of the school.
The SDBE MAT Board of TrusteesRetains overall legal accountability for the Trust and delegates responsibilities through the Scheme of Delegation.
The Local Governing BodyProvides local governance, strategic oversight, challenge and assurance within the responsibilities delegated by the Trust.
The Executive HeadteacherProvides executive and strategic leadership for the school and is accountable within the Trust's leadership and governance framework.
The Head of SchoolLeads the day-to-day operational work of St James Hatcham, working closely with the Executive Headteacher and senior leadership team.
Individual governors do not manage the school or direct members of staff.
Our Christian foundation
St James Hatcham is proud to be a Church of England school.
Our Christian vision:
Raising learners in excellence and godly character
Love • Peace • Joy • Hope
are central to the life and work of our school.
Our Local Governing Body has an important role in ensuring that our Christian vision and character remain visible in the education, relationships, worship and opportunities we provide for our children.
Our Scheme of Delegation
The SDBE MAT Scheme of Delegation explains how responsibilities are distributed between the:
The level at which individual decisions are made is determined by the current Scheme of Delegation and associated Trust policies.
View the current St James Hatcham Scheme of Delegation
SDBEMAT - GOVERNANCE
Members of the Trust;
Board of Trustees;
Trust committees;
Chief Executive Officer and executive leaders;
Local Governing Body; and
school leadership.
Local Governing Body meetings
Meetings of the whole local governing body are known as Local Governing Body Meetings (LGB Meetings).
The LGB meets regularly throughout the academic year to consider the school's progress, priorities and the areas of responsibility delegated to it.
Approved minutes, agendas and papers considered at meetings are available for public inspection on request, subject to appropriate redaction or exclusion of confidential information.
Governance enquiries
For governance enquiries or requests for governance records, please contact:
School Officeadmin@st-jameshatcham.lewisham.sch.uk0208 692 4937

St James Hatcham CE Maths Intent
We want to help our children approach Maths challenges fearlessly with grit and purpose, enjoying the struggle that comes with reasoning and problem solving. We are committed to fostering a love of learning through Maths, valuing questions and the contribution of all pupils in order that every individual is motivated to achieve at the very highest level and at the greatest depths of understanding.
We actively encourage a mathematical growth mindset reminding out children that they learn through mistakes, deeper thinking and challenges.
Our calculation policy ensures all pupils are well equipped with progressive, efficient strategies for the four operations relevant to the age and stage at which they are working.
Our intent is for every pupil to gain a rich mathematical experience beginning during the early years and leaving our care as able and independent mathematicians who are able to calculate fluently, reason confidently and solve problems efficiently.
At St James Hatcham we aim to:
I love Maths because I am good at spotting the odd one out.
St James Hatcham CE Maths Implementation
Our Maths curriculum at St James is delivered with the support of the White Rose Maths scheme and calculation policy. The models and images provided by the scheme help to support the understanding of mathematical concepts. This scheme supports a teaching approach that encourages new learning but also adopts a culture of ‘Revisit, Revise, Remember’ that promotes retention of knowledge and supports children to embed prior learning, make connections to current maths and consider future application.
The scheme breaks down the national curriculum objectives into smaller steps providing a scaffold for achievement with the small steps being connected and concepts being built upon. With the support of the scheme, teachers are able to deliver well-structured and thought provoking maths helping our children to progressively develop their skills at an age and stage appropriate level and supports with .
Teachers promote and encourage pupils to work collaboratively, as well as independently, and provide excellent modelling of all mathematical processes and concepts as part of everyday teaching through a ‘My turn, Our Turn, Your Turn’ approach. Our classroom environments provide visual consistency across key stages with learning walls promoting the concrete, pictorial and abstract approach as a guide and reference for our children. The walls provide access to current toolkits, prior learning, mathematical sentence stems to support with reasoning and a consistent problem solving strategy.
Alongside our consistent scheme, use of resources and environments, we adopt a consistent assessment approach using PiXL (Partners in Excellence). We use PiXL as a diagnostic tool and as support with data and tracking of progress to provide us with clear, concise information further aiding learning and achievement of mathematics at St James.
When I make a mistake it's ok because I can fix it and learn.
St James Hatcham CE Maths Impact
At St James, all pupils make good or better progress in maths.
Through evaluation of work in children’s books, it is clear to see the high quality of mathematics throughout St James. Children can confidently talk about their work in maths lessons and can apply age-appropriate skills and knowledge in their work. They aren’t afraid to make mistakes, recognising that mistakes help them to learn and challenges help their brains to grow demonstrating both perseverance and resilience in their mathematical learning. Our children enjoy Maths and understand its importance in the real world.

Music
Music
Music is fully embedded into school life at St James Hatcham as we aim to provide a platform for all our musicians to shine and develop their musical talents and potential.
It is proven that children who engage in high quality, regular musical learning from an early age gain musical, intellectual, emotional and social advantages. However, many children miss out on these benefits without access to high quality music education. Staff at St James Hatcham value singing, musical techniques, instrumental learning and the importance of a strong musicianship foundation.
We are extremely proud to partner with Stretto Music to deliver fun, enriching, and engaging music lessons across our school.
"Stretto Music delivers exceptional quality music specialists for EYFS, KS1 and KS2 in schools across London and the South East.
Music has a strong positive impact on the lives of children and makes them feel confident. Music instruction is documented to accelerate brain development in children, particularly in the areas of the brain responsible for processing sound, language development, speech perception and reading skills. It is important to have music as part of your school’s curriculum. Working as a musical team unites children and builds community."

Music
Music
Music is fully embedded into school life at St James Hatcham as we aim to provide a platform for all our musicians to shine and develop their musical talents and potential.
Come, let us sing for joy to the LORD; let us shout aloud to the Rock of our salvation.
It is proven that children who engage in high quality, regular musical learning from an early age gain musical, intellectual, emotional and social advantages. However, many children miss out on these benefits without access to high quality music education. Staff at St James Hatcham value singing, musical techniques, instrumental learning and the importance of a strong musicianship foundation.
We are extremely proud to partner with Stretto Music to deliver fun, enriching, and engaging music lessons across our school.
"Stretto Music delivers exceptional quality music specialists for EYFS, KS1 and KS2 in schools across London and the South East.
Music has a strong positive impact on the lives of children and makes them feel confident. Music instruction is documented to accelerate brain development in children, particularly in the areas of the brain responsible for processing sound, language development, speech perception and reading skills. It is important to have music as part of your school’s curriculum. Working as a musical team unites children and builds community."
Many of our pupils are actively involved in music and there is a wide range of opportunities to play, sing, perform or simply enjoy listening to music through:
Specialist teaching and training
In 2023 we were the only school in Lewisham to have partnered with The Voices Foundation, a national charity which aims to make sure that no child is left out when it comes to learning singing and musicianship. The Voices Foundation has provided training for all our school staff, developing their knowledge, skills and confidence in teaching music effectively. This has transformed the quality of music teaching in our school.
Singing and The Choir
Run by Mr Pryor and Ms Duffy, our pupils audition to be part of our highly successful choir who regularly perform for our school and wider community, sing at local events such as the legendary Lewisham Showcase and Turning of the Year.
We regularly incorporate various singing styles during our singing assemblies such as acapella, rounds and explore all aspects of musicianship. The qualities of musicianship work alongside our whole school vision of developing oracy and becoming confident, articulate in performance.
Singing has become an everyday norm here at St James Hatcham and our children’s talents shine through all aspects of the school day.
Instrumental tuition
Lessons are offered in a range of instruments, including piano, drumming and guitar, of which the majority take place during the school day. There is a charge for instrumental tuition, but the cost is much lower than private lessons outside school and are subsidised for pupils in receipt of pupil premium funding or for SEND pupils with an Education, Health and Care Plan.
Following enthusiastic participation in instrumental tuition here at St James Hatcham, Kason was nominated by his tutor and subsequently awarded a full scholarship with Lewisham Music Fund, funding further 1:1 lessons and access to the the Saturday Music Centre. This month Kason was also awarded their 'Scholar of the month' who aspires to play the guitar like Jimi Hendrix one day!
We see, nurture and develop musical talent in all pupils.
The Piatti Quartet
Through the Cavatina Music Trust, the Piatti Quartet have performed regularly at St James Hatcham. They are one of the most distinguished string quartets of their generation and have performed in all the major venues and festivals around the country and abroad. Their recitals give our children an opportunity to hear world-class classical music performed live in their own school. We are very fortunate that quartet member, Michael Trainor has been one of our regular violin tutors.
The Gentlemen of St John's
The Gentlemen of St John's are a vocal ensemble made up of Choral and Organ Scholars from the Choir of St John’s College, Cambridge. We are extremely lucky to receive visits from The ‘Gents’ who perform and provide workshops for our pupils.
